title: sedum rosea var. integrifolium
intro: Sedum rosea var. integrifolium, commonly known as Rose Sedum or White Stonecrop, is a succulent plant species native to Europe and Asia, characterized by its white flowers and narrow, linear leaves. The plant is used in traditional medicine due to its reported health benefits, which include treating fever, sore throat, and skin conditions, as well as aiding in the regulation of blood pressure and digestion. The therapeutic actions of Sedum rosea var. integrifolium are attributed to its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antibacterial properties, which help to soothe and protect the skin and mucous membranes. The bioactive constituents of the plant include triterpenoid saponins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
